Since Kalinskaya was at that time in a relationship with Jannik Sinner, whom the Canberran has repeatedly pointed out since it was learned that Sinner failed two drug tests last spring, the comment was widely interpreted as a vulgar blow to the couple.
While Kyrgios refused to prepare beyond denying the comment, he was abusive, the 29 -year -old has been considerably closer in his feelings about Sinner, who faces an arbitration court for the sports audience in April in which the World Agency Anti -doping will argue should be excluded from the game for up to two years.

The years between these two incidents brought an extensive catalog of fines, controversy and minor crimes, including a disqualification in Rome in 2019, when he launched a chair on the entire court, and a series of spike comments about his contemporaries, including Novak Djokovic , with whom he has formed a close friendship, and Nadal.
Only this week, Kyrgios entered the debate after Goncalo Oliveira of Venezuela was provisionally suspended by a positive test of methamphetamine. “The steroids are fine, but this is wild,” he subtitled an Instagram post.

Pointing out that his compatriot Max Purcell had been provisionally suspended after admitting a violation of the anti -doping rules, Kyrgios also accused the authorities of double ratings, which suggests that the high -profile stars such as Sinner and Swiatek were treated more lightly.

However, none of those mentioned has continued to fix the sinner in the same degree as Kyrgios, and the sensation persists among many in the sport that the apparent antipathy of the Australian is based on the relationship of Italian with Kalinskaya.
“This is just a personal revenge,” said American tennis analyst Jon Wertheim last month on Andy Roddick’s podcast. ‘There is a woman involved here, who is also a player. Sinner has been relentlessly intimidated for months and months and has not responded.
‘There are so many things here, but it seems to have anything to do with good faith concerns about doping.
‘(Kyrgios) did not even seem to understand the doping protocols and the context to begin with, which leads me to conclude that all this is only … Against a player who is now dating an ex -girlfriend and nothing more.’
Time will say, in case it is speculated that Sinner and Kalinskaya have divided well founded.
The relationship was subject to scrutiny in the last months of last year after Sinner commented in a magazine interview that having a girlfriend “is something that makes you feel good or makes you feel bad.” Subsequently, the rumors swirled that the couple had stopped continuing on social networks.
Forced from the Australian Open at the 11th hour after contracting a virus, Kalinskaya was absent from the Sinner box while collecting its third important title in Melbourne, a marked contrast with the scenes that followed the final of Us Open last September, When the couple shared a kiss after the Italian victory over Taylor Fritz.
Like Sinner, Kalinskaya has refused to be attracted to the controversy, but it seemed to give Kyrgios the cold shoulder when the two crossings crossed behind the scene in Melbourne Park.
There seems to be little love lost everywhere, and former Wimbledon champion, Marion Bartoli, is among those who feel enough is enough.
“Kyrgios lives and breathes for this, to make more and more provocative statements,” Bartoli told the RMC Sport French television channel.
‘This is a player who was able to say absolute horrors to Stan Wawrinka, who is one of the most educated, most loved and most respected players on a tennis court, in a 1000 masters in the middle of a game.
